correctness.rationale: On these simple cubic graphs, being on a side with no isolated vertex is exactly the cross-degree bound of two. For fixed labelled columns, a colouring determines one walk on ordered pairs of column symbols; the ordinary and crossed closures are respectively the endpoints s and Js, where J swaps both rows. Thus tr(U^n) and tr(U^nJ) count labelled ordered assignments, not cyclic orbits, with both seam vertices checked even at n=3. I reconstructed U, used exact nullspaces of J±I and an exact change of basis to check its two characteristic polynomials: x^4(x^2+2)(x^4−3x^3−x^2+2), x^4(x^2−x+1). Newton sums give the stated A,B,C initial values and recurrences; signs are +C for the prism, −C for Möbius. Removing two constant assignments and dividing by two for free global complement gives the stated counts. Direct vertex-colouring enumeration at n=3,4,5,6 gave (16,18),(58,59),(181,180),(581,579). In the structural proof, a simultaneous row swap from just after the last monochromatic rung to the seam moves the twist to that rung; its centers already have a same-colour partner, and its neighbours see identical entries across that interface. This also works if the monochromatic rung is the last column (the switch is vacuous). Only the all-mixed words contribute to the difference; their adjacent-bit transfer forbids a middle bit unequal to both neighbours, and the complement-odd block has polynomial x^2−x+1. This gives the exact period-six seam difference, whereas all-monochromatic-rung assignments already give at least 2^{n−1}−1 valid unordered nonempty cuts for each ladder. The matrix calculation and local bijection prove the all-order claim, not the finite graph samples.

evidence: Gomes–Sau define d-cuts by the per-vertex cross-degree bound. On a cubic graph, a defensive alliance in the sense d_in+1≥d_out requires d_in≥1, so the same cuts are exactly partitions into two such alliances.
Kwon–Park–Sano require every vertex to have neighbours in both parts; b9c77d1b74ba requires a unique plurality of the vertex's own colour.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The two-alliance and no-isolate formulations really are equivalent; coupon colouring requires an additional opposite neighbour, and strict binary plurality requires at least two same-side neighbours. Neither of those cited stronger constraints counts all these cuts.

value.rationale: A cut constraint with a direct graph meaning is compared under the natural untwisted/twisted closures of the same strip; exact absolute counts are useful test cases and the difference stays uniformly bounded despite exponential growth. The seam switch gives a structural reason: every configuration with a protective monochromatic rung cancels, leaving only the odd spectrum of a four-state system. This is more than a different presentation of a known chromatic or majority count.
